# How we work here

Two databases, two questions. **Systems** answers *what is there*. **Tasks** answers *what has to be done*. Everything else is a page.

## Every task hangs off a system

A task with no system is invisible: the system does not see its own work and the progress column does not count it. If a task fits no system yet, the system is the thing that is missing — add it first.

## The title names the symptom, not the fix

"A 24 MB upload took the instance down" — not "add an upload limit". The symptom stays true after the fix and is what somebody searches for a year later. The fix belongs in the page.

## Decisions go in the page, including the ones you dropped

Write down what you decided and why, and write down what you decided *against*. Nobody ever asks why something was not built — which is exactly why it gets proposed a second time.

## Set the status before you start, not after

*In progress* is a statement about now. Set afterwards it is a diary entry, and while it is missing everyone else assumes the task is free.

## Technical documentation stays in the repository

What belongs here is what you want to know *without* the code in front of you: status, where it runs, which decisions were taken, what is still open. Nothing kept in two places.

## Big things are bundled by milestone

Several tasks sharing one milestone text — not a folder, not a chain of sub-pages. A folder hides the work from the board it belongs on.

## Never put a password, token or key on a page

A pointer to where it lives is fine. The page is searchable, exportable and shareable, and one of those will eventually happen to it.
